messages:
Maya: quick heads-up — ran the AWQ vs FP8 prefetched bake today on llama‑like-13b. baseline fp8 + prefetch + continuous batching looked stable. awq + prefetch + continuous shows consistent quality dip on our eval set (small instruction-following tasks). EM down ~3.4% abs, BLEU -2.1, p99 up ~35ms, KV cache hit-rate down ~12%.
Sam: ouch. any config diffs besides quant backend?
Maya: same model weights, same tokenizer. only changed quantizer (awq vs fp8/gptq) and enabled awq’s packer. experiment commands: ```python tools/eval.py --model models/llama-13b:rev-2026-02 --quant awq --prefetch enabled --batching mode=continuous,max_wait_ms=12 --eval-set eval/inst-follow.jsonl```
Liam: can you paste a short example where it regresses? is it hallucinating or just lower exact-match?
Maya: mostly hallucination on factual Qs and occasional truncation mid-answer (early stop). EM drop is concentrated in multi-step reasoning prompts. example: question about process steps -> awq answers skip step 2.
Ana: interesting — could be KV cache staleness + quantized attention weights causing prefix mismatch when prefetch reuses KV between requests. did you check prefix alignment / seqhash?
Maya: good call. seqhash mismatch rate is slightly higher on AWQ runs (we track mismatch when prefetched key len differs). attached numbers: seqhash_mismatch: fp8=0.4% awq=1.9%.
Sam: possible handshake/kv-handoff race when continuous batching merges heterogeneous seq lengths + awq’s packer repacks tokens -> cache entries point to wrong key length bucket. we saw similar in past with int8 packing.
Liam: can you rerun with prefetch disabled but same batching to isolate cache vs quantizer?
Maya: doing that now. expected finish in ~30m.
ops-bot: deploy notice — started a shadow run on dedicated-shadow-3 for thread 2190012345 at 2026-03-20T09:10:00Z.
Ana: also try: lower continuous batching max_wait to 6ms and increase pack alignment tolerance (kv_tolerance=2). if mismatch fixes, it's cache-handshake. if not, AWQ may have attention kernel numerical edge-case with long-prefix keys.
Sam: also capture token-level logits / top-k diffs for the first 50 tokens after prefix boundary. small numeric drift early can cascade. we can diff logits via `tools/logdiff --base fp8-run/ --cmp awq-run/ --topk 20 --prefix-boundary`
Maya: added that to the job. quick preliminary: when prefetch disabled, EM drop shrinks to 0.6% and p99 returns close to baseline. suggests prefetch+awq interaction.
Liam: ok that narrows it. do we have candidate mitigations? 1) disable prefetch for awq models in prod; 2) increase prefetch TTL to avoid stale replacements; 3) force rekey on packer change so cache keys include quant schema fingerprint; 4) tune continuous batching thresholds.
Ana: rank by ops impact: (1) add quant-fingerprint in kv-key (low perf cost), (2) toggle prefetch per-model (config flag), (3) adjust TTL and batching if needed.
Sam: adding a quick experiment: change kv key from `model:rev:seqhash` to `model:rev:quant-fp:seqhash` so awq-prefetch won’t match fp8 entries. low-risk.
Maya: ran that locally — cache hit rate on awq-run drops (expected), but EM recovers to baseline because no stale cross-quant hits. p99 slightly worse due to missed cache but still within SLA.
Liam: tradeoff seems acceptable if cost delta small. we can A/B route small % traffic and measure cost/unit. what about canary rollout plan?
Ana: propose: 1) patch kv key to include quant fingerprint and deploy to canary (5%), 2) observe EM, p99, cost over 48h, 3) if OK, promote and then enable prefetch+awq for wider scale. fallback policy: if EM regresses >1% or p99 > +50ms => rollback.
Sam: I'll push a small PR to add quant_fingerprint to kv key and a flag to allow per-model prefetch. assigning to @Maya for canary monitoring.
Maya: ack. starting canary config now. will post results in this thread. thanks for the triage. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: canary rollout started: service=inference, config=kv-key-quant-fp-canary, pct=5, start=2026-03-20T09:42:00Z.
Maya: quick note for docs/ops — adding a short blurb in runbook about quant-aware cache keying + prefetched model exceptions.
Liam: nice. also file a follow-up to check AWQ packer PRs for any kernel changes that affect attention numerics — ping infra-ml.
Ana: agree. if canary shows cost spike, we can explore hybrid: prefetch for fp8, disable prefetch for awq until packer stable.
Maya: thanks team. I'll paste canary metrics once we have 6h and 24h snapshots. closing for now but will reopen if regressions appear. :white_check_mark:
